b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's first doorbell, HL · Website hook → email.

Trigger: Webhooks by Zapier · Catch Hook (not Raw). Copy the URL; keep it out of chats and screenshots.

Send it from Hoppscotch: POST, header Content-Type: application/json, body = the good order HL-0051. Then click Test trigger.

What Zapier shows:

FieldSample value
tokenhl-web-7Q2x
order_idHL-0051
customer__nameMrs Adebayo
customer__phone+2348031234567
items__sku / items__qty / items__unit_priceline-item fields holding both items, often shown joined: TOM-CRATE,PEP-TATASHE-L
delivery_fee / total1500 / 35500

Action: Gmail · Send Email to yourself. Subject: Website order [order_id]. Body: Customer: [customer__name], Phone: [customer__phone], Total sent by website: [total]. Never map token into an email.

One-sentence explanation: "The double underscore shows nesting: customer__phone is the phone field inside the customer object, which in 0.3's path notation is customer.phone."

Log note: the total here is only what the website claims; Silver recalculates it.
mistakes: Choosing Catch Raw Hook, so there are no flattened fields to map.
Leaving out the Content-Type header, so the JSON arrives as one unparsed blob.
Clicking Test trigger before sending a request, then mapping from empty sample data.
Putting the token or the hook URL into the email, log or a screenshot.
b.pass: The email arrives with three mapped fields from the hook (e.g. order_id, customer__name, customer__phone), and the learner's sentence correctly says the double underscore means a field nested inside another object.
b.redo: Send it back if the fields were typed in by hand, the hook URL or token is visible in the evidence, or the explanation of the double underscore is wrong.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's checked website order line, built exactly as the solved problem (Catch Raw Hook → Code → Paths → Sheets or alert), with Order_Items filled from line_items.

Expected results for all requests:

RequestWhat was sentExpected outcome
Good order HL-00512 items, total 35500Orders row (items_total 34000, fee 1500, total 35500) + 2 Order_Items rows
Edited total HL-005210 crates, total 11Alert: total mismatch: sent 11, calculated 126500
No token, bad qty HL-0053qty "two", no phoneAlert: wrong or missing token; missing phone; item 1: bad qty
Broken JSONtrailing comma, no closing braceAlert: body is not valid JSON; wrong or missing token; missing phone; no items
Own bad 1 HL-0056unit_price 0, total 1500Alert: item 1: bad price
Own bad 2 HL-0057qty -2, total -23500Alert: item 1: bad qty
3-item order HL-0055TOM-CRATE 2 × 12500, PEP-TATASHE-L 1 × 9000, ONI-BAG 3 × 4000, fee 1500, total 475001 Orders row (total 47500) + 3 Order_Items rows

Check by hand: 25000 + 9000 + 12000 = 46000; plus 1500 = 47500. 10 × 12500 + 1500 = 126500.

Comparison: Orders has exactly 2 new rows (HL-0051, HL-0055); Order_Items has 5; the inbox has 5 rejection emails, each naming the right reasons. Zap history shows the 5 invalid runs going down the fallback branch.

The secret in Input Data is fine for practice; in a real build it's a long random string, shared only with the developer.
mistakes: Returning line_items as a bare list, so the Orders row is created once per item.
Branch A rule checks valid as text "true" instead of (Boolean) Is true, so nothing passes.
Only sending the four given samples, or inventing "bad" requests that are actually valid.
Never sending a 3-item order, so the one-row/three-rows check is untested.
s.pass: Orders contains only the valid orders, every invalid request produced an alert listing the correct reasons, and a 3-item order created exactly one Orders row and three Order_Items rows.
s.redo: Send it back if any invalid request reached the sheet, an alert has missing or wrong reasons, or the Order_Items count doesn't match the items sent.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane passing valid website orders to a courier, played by a webhook.site URL.

1. Add the address to the test payload (the samples have none): "customer": { "name": "Mrs Adebayo", "phone": "+2348031234567", "address": "14 Adeoyo Street", "area": "Ring Road" }. In the main Code step, add address and area to output, read from order.customer.

2. Code step "Courier message" (valid branch only). Input Data: order_id, item_count, area, phone.

const area = String(inputData.area || "").trim() || "area not given";
const message = `${inputData.order_id} · ${inputData.item_count} items · ${area} · call ${inputData.phone}`;
output = { message };

3. Webhooks by Zapier · POST "Notify courier":

FieldSet to
URLyour webhook.site URL
Payload Typejson
Dataorder_id, phone, address, item_count, message (pills from the Code steps)
HeadersX-Source | harvest-lane

What webhook.site shows for the 3-item test order:

POST  x-source: harvest-lane
{ "order_id": "HL-0055", "phone": "+2348031234567",
  "address": "14 Adeoyo Street", "item_count": "3",
  "message": "HL-0055 · 3 items · Ring Road · call +2348031234567" }

Evidence to submit: webhook.site screenshots for each valid order (header visible), a Zap history screenshot of an invalid order showing the fallback branch and no POST, and a log line: "6 requests sent, 2 valid, 2 courier requests received, 0 for invalid". Use test data only: webhook.site URLs can be viewed by anyone who has them.
mistakes: Putting the POST step before Paths, so invalid orders are sent to the courier too.
Expecting an address field the samples never contained, so the payload has a blank address.
Typing the header into the Data field, so it arrives in the body instead of the headers.
Sending a real customer's name and phone to a public webhook.site URL.
g.pass: webhook.site shows one request per valid order carrying X-Source: harvest-lane and the WhatsApp-ready message, and Zap history proves invalid orders took the fallback with no POST.
g.redo: Send it back if the header is missing, any invalid order produced a courier request, or real customer data was sent to webhook.site.
